notes: [S006.N1] This typescript carries a faint upper-centre mark with no securely decipherable numeral; 5 remains an alternative. The separate bottom-left archive 5 is clear. There is no title, date or written total. It begins with the Hom display and ends with live obligerai- followed by a globally cancelled three-line block ending néces-. No unseen continuation is supplied on this page.

[S006.N2] The text calls the displayed Hom map an isomorphisme de catégories. It says Nous n’explicitons pas ici la construction and describes verification of toutes les compatibilités voulues as fort longue et fastidieuse. It names K^0 and K^1 as invariants of the enveloping category, identifies the finite-projective-module example with the cited classical invariants, and qualifies its additive-category extension by sans doute. The later passage says semblent rendre peu probable about a canonical derived complex and Il y a tout lieu de croire about higher Picard n-categories. These source qualifications are preserved, not upgraded to proofs.

[S006.N3] A limited logical check separates the canonical-complex heuristic from a contradiction. Under scan005’s stated classification data (pi_0, pi_1, s), matching pi_0 and pi_1 does not require matching s. A strict category with those same two groups need not be equivalent to the nonstrict category under discussion. Thus its existence alone would not contradict nonstrictness. This identifies the scope of the tentative argument; it neither proves nor refutes existence of a canonical derived complex.

[S006.N4] A separate counterexample tests the literal assertion that taking S to be all objects makes S^{-1}C a Picard category. The main crop confirms that unqualified wording. Let C have one object *, End(*)=(N,+), identity 0, composition addition, tensor on arrows addition, strict unit/associativity and identity symmetry. Addition is commutative, so interchange and symmetry naturality hold. The sole object is already tensor-invertible, making identity C->C a solution of the stated object-inversion universal property for S={*}. The arrow 1 has no inverse, so C is not a groupoid and fails the Picard requirement from scans002/004. This refutes the unrestricted implication as written. Refined statement S006.N4.object_invertibility_only: object-inversion ensures invertible objects, while a Picard conclusion also requires invertible morphisms or an additional hypothesis/construction supplying them. No unstated authorial convention is asserted, and no repair is made to the transcription.

[S006.N5] The crop settles interpétation without the second r in the first sentence of the final live paragraph, despite two readers’ half-image readings. It also settles the comma after somme), preserving capital Cela, and the old P beneath F. The upper second K degree touches the preceding pi_1 subscript: the live raised 1 and cancelled lower 1 are secure, but an older upper numeral is not. A high point/apostrophe after stricte) and a dot/weak-hyphen remnant at inversib/le are retained although both witnesses omit them. Plain chaines, que, cette, and all prospective wording remain as written.

[S006.N6] The completed three-reader run used fresh isolated readers after an initial snapshot-preparation error was caught. The first attempts had received trailing earlier-page doubt text and were abandoned; their status is documented, and none is used as a completed reading. The replacements received notation only. Main compared all three complete returns and inspected eleven reader B crops, one reader C crop and six new tight crops, eighteen distinct crops. Eight loci remain uncertain. No whole or half image was opened by the main reader.
